title: Capacity qualifier workshop and SLA decision ledger for enterprise dedicated requests
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Run a cross-functional capacity qualifier workshop that produces a single source-of-truth decision ledger mapping enterprise request fingerprints to SLA bands, recommended GPU classes, reserved throughput profiles, and autoscale guardrails.

Background: Sales and Solutions Engineering are seeing repeated enterprise asks that fall between our existing banded playbooks and ad-hoc concierge handling. We need a lightweight, reproducible rubric to: 1) accelerate intake conversations, 2) provide deterministic recommendations for GPU family and reserved throughput, and 3) produce a documented SLA target with fallback routing/scaling policies for engineering.

Deliverables (by end of workshop):
- Decision ledger (CSV + human-readable summary) that maps workload fingerprints (QPS, p50 latency target, max context length, model family, memory per request) to: SLA band (gold/silver/bronze), suggested GPU class (H100/A100/L40s tier mapping), reserved throughput (tokens/sec and concurrent sessions), and recommended autoscale parameters (min/max pool size, burst credit policy, preemption tolerance).
- A short decision rubric (3–5 gating questions) and intake checklist for Solutions Engineering to use in first customer call.
- One sample customer intake run (redacted) that goes from questionnaire -> recommended SLA band -> expected monthly cost estimate.
- Engineering acceptance criteria for automated recommendation prototyping (set of 6 inputs, expected output structure, API contract).

Scope & out-of-scope:
- In scope: policy for SLA targets, GPU class mapping, reserved throughput bands, autoscaling guardrails for Dedicated pools.
- Out of scope: billing contract language, legal SLAs, and private/VPC network design.

Key trade-offs to document during workshop:
- Aggressive latency SLOs vs reserved throughput cost (when to recommend higher GPU class vs larger reservation).
- Heterogeneous pool routing complexity vs predictable single-GPU selection.
- Conservative burst credit policies (protect capacity) vs customer experience during spiky inference patterns.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ledger produced and uploaded to Confluence + CSV exported to drive.
- Engineering accepts the rubric as a clear input spec for PM-led prototype.
- Sales/SE sign-off that rubric reduces intake time and produces a credible cost estimate within 10% of manual concierge quotes.

Artifacts & links:
- Workshop notes & ledger: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DC/Capacity+Qualifier+Workshop
- Prototype API contract notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBc_example_contract
- Related runtime PR (context for burst policy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6321
- SLA observability dashboard (sample metrics): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/enterprise/sla-guidance

Stakeholders: Sales (reps: Jenna Morris), Solutions Eng (lead: Marco Santos), Infra/Runtime Eng (owner: Linh Nguyen), Reliability (owner: Mateo Ruiz), Legal (FYI: Rachel Bloom).
